match_note: Several first-round references to specific content match arXiv v1. These include line 55 'LSMO(12 nm)/NNO(0, 4, 8 and 16 nm)', the line 135 parenthetical '(full scans for all temperatures are plotted in the supplementary section)', and lines 242-244 'These emergent behaviours, driven by structural and magnetic reconstructions at the interface'. Also matching are the phrase 'AFM insulating domains within a much larger metallic matrix', the Δα/αLSMO definition, Fig. 1a/1b not being referenced individually, and the Fig. S5 Ms vs T data. v1 lacks material the rebuttal says was added in revision: RSXS domain data, RSM maps, EELS concentration profile, XAS, warming-cycle damping, the carrier-lifetime and spin-transparency calculations, and 'epitaxial' in the main title. One small discrepancy: v1 already cites Safi (ref 59) and Kim (ref 65) in a sentence noting that VO2 shows no enhancement at TMIT, whereas R1 said Safi was cited only for YIG/Pt. Supplementary figure numbering in v1 is internally inconsistent (text refers to S3 for the R-T derivative figure labelled S6). R4 was an early-career co-reviewer with no separate comments. R3's report was an attached file, which the authors answered under the heading 'Reviewer #4'. R5 joined at the third round.

concerns.quote: is limited by the fact that the metal-insulator transition temperature of NdNiO3 is well below room temperature.
concerns.summary: The claimed relevance for energy-efficient spintronic devices is undermined because the NNO MIT occurs well below room temperature.

concerns.quote: the idea of monitoring S2CC across the phase transition of the "converter" element is not new, with several reports available
concerns.summary: Tracking spin-to-charge conversion across a phase transition has already been reported (VO2, Ta, Sb2Te3), and the VO2 result in particular is not discussed or compared.

concerns.quote: the authors should convincingly report about the possible variation of the chemical-structural-magnetic properties for the LSMO in their set of sample, since that could heavily impact the extracted S2CC efficiency.
concerns.summary: It is unclear whether the reference LSMO film has the same properties as the LSMO in the bilayers, which matters for the Δα used to extract spin mixing conductance and spin Hall angle.

concerns.quote: contextualizing the presented results about S2CC efficiency with those obtained in other systems of recent high interest, such as topological insulators, transition metal dichalcogenides
concerns.summary: The S2CC efficiencies should be compared with other high-interest systems and with other phase-transition S2CC studies.

concerns.quote: Probing the domain formation in these devices would greatly enhance the understanding especially towards the microscopic picture.
concerns.summary: The proposed mechanism (sparse AFM insulating domains acting as scatterers) is not directly probed, and estimates of domain size or the critical domain size are needed.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the article lacks a neat result and is rather descriptive in nature. We believe that a deeper analysis of the experimental results is necessary
concerns.summary: The work is largely descriptive and lacks a clear microscopic picture of the spin-charge conversion enhancement. R2 makes the same point: the manuscript 'lacks clarity in the microscopic picture'.

concerns.quote: The overall impact of this work on the field is not highlighted enough... the discussion should be enhanced by stating how this methodology can be used to develop other devices.
concerns.summary: The broader impact and the device implications of the methodology are not adequately articulated.

concerns.quote: the discussion (for example, lines 236-244) struggles to pinpoint the ways this system is uniquely suited to enhance spin-to-charge conversion.
concerns.summary: The discussion lists generic oxide properties instead of saying what makes this system special, which other systems could host the effect, or how it could be enhanced.

concerns.quote: given the importance of strain in this central claim of the paper, it would be important to present reciprocal space map measurements
concerns.summary: Reciprocal space maps are needed to confirm the epitaxial and strain state of the bilayer, beyond the 2θ XRD shown.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: In view of figure 3 (a), it seems that in both phases have the same spin-to-charge or magnon-to-charge efficiency. Thus, it is not evident to us that at the transition, the presence of insulating phase domains would enhance this efficiency.
concerns.summary: The metallic (spin) and insulating (magnon) phases appear to give similar conversion in Fig. 3(a), so the claim that insulating domains enhance efficiency at the transition is not convincing.

concerns.quote: The manuscript is a bit confusing and needs of an improvement of the presentation.
concerns.summary: The overall presentation is confusing and needs improvement.

concerns.quote: Figures 1a and 1b are not referenced in the main text.
concerns.summary: Figure panels 1a and 1b are not cited in the text.

concerns.quote: The nomenclature for the LSMO without NNO on top is rather confusing.
concerns.summary: Labelling the single LSMO layer as NNO(0) is confusing and should be separated from the bilayers.

concerns.quote: The existence of the hysteresis loop in the x=4 nm bilayer is not clear as it gets easily confused with the x=16 nm curve.
concerns.summary: The hysteresis of the 4 nm NNO bilayer in Fig. 1 is not visible, and the colours should be improved.

concerns.quote: The crossing point of the derivative with the y=0 axis is not clear at all, especially seeing the noise that is present around 150 K.
concerns.summary: The dR/dT zero crossing used to define TMIT in Fig. S3(c) is ambiguous given the noise.

concerns.quote: This should point to the specific supplementary figure it is referring to.
concerns.summary: The line 135 reference to the supplementary full scans should name the specific figure.

concerns.quote: the spin to charge conversion is measured using the cooling cycle... Some measurements or discussion about the heating cycle would add value to the manuscript.
concerns.summary: Only cooling-cycle SP-FMR data are shown, and warming-cycle data or discussion are needed given the hysteretic transition and the spin-valve claims.

concerns.quote: "These emergent behaviours, driven by structural and magnetic reconstructions at the interface,..." This paragraph lacks explanation or citations.
concerns.summary: The claims about interfacial reconstructions in the discussion are unsupported by explanation or references.

concerns.quote: even at 100ºC nickelates develop oxygen vacancies [1]... XPS stochiometry measurements would be useful to check if the O pressure is sufficient.
concerns.summary: Oxygen stoichiometry of NNO after the 710 °C anneal should be verified, for example by XPS.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: A brief description of how the samples were transferred to the different fabrication and measurement chambers would be adequate, as long exposures to air can lead to carbon accumulation
concerns.summary: Methods should describe sample transfer and air exposure, which could add extrinsic spin scattering.

later_concerns.quote: what worries me are the VSM data in Fig.S5, from where it is clear tha the magnetic properties of the LSMO alone are not overalpping those in the coupled LSMO/NNO.
later_concerns.summary: In round 2, the reference LSMO (grown and annealed differently) has different magnetization from the bilayer LSMO, which may invalidate Δα and the S2CC estimate.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: the study remains largely descriptive and does not provide sufficient microscopic insight or conceptual novelty to justify publication in Nature Communications.
later_concerns.summary: In round 2, the work is technically sound but insufficiently novel or insightful for the journal, and better suited to a specialised journal.

later_concerns.quote: the manuscript currently falls short of the level of explanation, typically supported by some form of calculation, expected for publication at this level.
later_concerns.summary: In round 3, the interpretation lacks quantitative or calculational support.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: the statement that the work "provides new insights into the interplay of the NNO phase transition with the LSMO magnetization dynamics" (line 86) is not fully supported by the presented data.
later_concerns.summary: In round 3, claims are overstated, and supporting them would require LSMO thickness or doping studies.

later_concerns.quote: The R(T) data (Supplementary Fig. S3) show a broad transition with no clear hysteresis, suggesting that the film may not be of "optimal" quality
later_concerns.summary: In round 3, the broad, weakly hysteretic MIT suggests suboptimal NNO, and the role of disorder and phase coexistence in the results should be discussed.

first_round.quote: While I fully recognize that this is the first report of S2CC in NdNiO3 across its phase transition, due to the above considerations I do not see this manuscript significant enough for Nature Communications.
it would be important to present reciprocal space map measurements... If these revisions cannot be made, I would recommend this publication be sent out to a more specialized journal.
the article lacks a neat result and is rather descriptive in nature. We believe that a deeper analysis of the experimental results is necessary in order to claim an important, novel result
I co-reviewed this manuscript with one of the reviewers who provided the listed reports.

recommendations.note: There is no sign of a transfer from another journal; Version 0 is treated as the first round. R1 gave no formal verdict, but the 'not significant enough for Nature Communications' statement is read as reject. R3's report was an attached file (pages 37-38). R4 only states that they co-reviewed with one of the other referees. R4 is given R3's recommendation because the authors' rebuttal answers the attached R3 report under the Reviewer #4 heading, and that report uses 'we/us'. R5 did not take part in the first round: they joined at Version 2 and asked for revision with moderated claims. R5 is therefore not listed.
recommendations.label: contested
